analysis: Examined ProviderLoop+ModelLoading.swift (head lines 1-1043). Changes: (1) the weight hasher is now an injectable `loadWeightHasher` captured into the detached task (lines 47, 60, 76, 78) instead of calling WeightHasher.computeHash directly. Output is still routed through SSDPrefixCacheFactory.verifiedWeightHash, so the fail-closed validation is kept. The definition and default value of loadWeightHasher are outside the supplied evidence; if it is test-only and defaults to WeightHasher.computeHash there is no regression, and production initialisation should be confirmed (T-012, T-027, T-041). (2) `artifactIdentityRequired` (lines 546-549) now forces a fresh cryptographic pre-load hash and a post-load hash (lines 556-563, 624-635) for the GLM plan, reusable SSD, and the serving/deadline performance profiles. The pre-load hash is published only when identity is not required. Publication happens after the pre/post equality check via finalizeReusableSSDLoad, which unloads on a mismatch (.changed) and disables the SSD cache on .unavailable. `cacheEligibleWeightHash` is set only when reusableSSDRequested, so a performance-profile-only load gets a verified artifact hash but no cache key. This is consistent with the T-041 hash binding and fail-closed intent. (3) GLM managed path (lines 615-623) uses verifiedGLM5NextWeightHash with pre=post=verified, which relies on the managed loader's per-file SHA verification and the recheck at 554. The glmIdentitiesBeforeLoad vs post-load comparison happens in recordVerifiedGLM5NextWeightHash, whose body is outside the supplied evidence. (4) The non-identity-required fallback path (636-655) sets cacheEligibleWeightHash=nil, so no cache reuse from a fingerprint-only check. Remaining questions for integration: the loadWeightHasher definition, verifiedGLM5NextWeightHash and recordVerifiedGLM5NextWeightHash behaviour, and the unseen tail of the patch. No concrete security regression is identified.
